page: Vultr vbm-8c-128gb-amd is a bare metal server featuring an AMD EPYC 4345P processor built on the x86_64 architecture. This dedicated system provides 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The processor includes 32 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, alongside cryptography standards like AES and SHA_NI. The server is equipped with 123.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, yielding 7.71 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 3890 GB NVMe SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU is included.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU metrics, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all scoring in the top 10% of tested systems. Passmark memory scores also rank in the top 10%, reflecting the high-frequency DDR5 memory. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core CPU and Passmark CPU scores, falls within the average range. For language model workloads, the server achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 414.79 tokens per second on small 135M models, though performance scales down to average levels for medium 7B models. A notable performance tradeoff is observed in large-block memory write bandwidth, which ranks in the bottom 25% at 21.89 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this bare metal server offers high resource density by combining dedicated EPYC CPU cores with a substantial 123.0 GB DDR5 memory footprint and nearly 3.9 TB of local NVMe storage. This hardware profile is suited for workloads requiring dedicated physical resources without virtualization overhead. Appropriate use cases include database hosting, memory-intensive applications, static web serving, and single-threaded data processing tasks that benefit from the server's strong single-core performance and fast local storage.
